The story

Orient's origins trace back to 1901 when Shogoro Yoshida opened the Yoshida Watch Shop in Tokyo. After establishing a clock and then a wristwatch manufacturing facility, the company was officially founded as the Tama Keiki Company in 1950, changing its name to Orient Watch Co., Ltd. in 1951. That same year, the brand launched its iconic and more refined Orient Star line. Throughout its history, Orient has focused on in-house mechanical movements, a commitment that helped it navigate the quartz crisis of the 1970s. The brand developed significant calibers, including the Cal. 46 series in 1971, which became the foundation for many of its modern movements. Orient is known for a variety of styles, from the elegant Bambino and its Small Seconds variations to sporty dive watches like the Kamasu and Triton. The brand also frequently features Open Heart designs that display the movement. In 2009, Orient became a wholly owned subsidiary of Seiko Epson, though it continues to operate as a distinct brand, manufacturing its own movements and watches in Japan. This relationship has allowed Orient to leverage greater resources while maintaining its identity for craftsmanship and value. Today, Orient and its premier Orient Star line are respected for their blend of traditional watchmaking, enduring style, and accessibility.
